title: Selective coupling of high-order phonons in La2-xSrxCuO4
authors: Ke-Jun Xu, Paulina Majchrzak, Nathan Giles-Donovan, Sangheon Kim, Jaewon Choi, Jun Okamoto, Ganesha Channagowdra, Hsiao-Yu Huang, Di-Jing Huang, Seiki Komiya, Takao Sasagawa, Shuichi Wakimoto, Wei-Sheng Lee, Zhi-Xun Shen, Thomas P. Devereaux, Dung-Hai Lee, Robert J. Birgeneau
abstract: In crystals and molecules with strong coupling between the charge carriers and atomic vibrations, high order harmonics of the vibrational excitations can be observed with intensity following the Franck-Condon envelope. Here, we uncover a new regime of electron-phonon coupling in La2-xSrxCuO4 using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. In the undoped compound, we find sharp peaks at approximately 85$\pm$5 meV, 180$\pm$7 meV, and 330$\pm$5 meV with no observable dispersion, and an absence of appreciable intensity from other modes observed in Raman spectroscopy in this energy range. The 180 meV and 330 meV excitations have energies approximately consistent with two-phonon and four-phonon in-plane Cu-O bond stretching mode, suggesting that the resonantly excited valence electrons strongly couple to this mode. These excitations exhibit significant doping dependence, eventually becoming unresolvable at 10% hole doping, where the low energy charge excitations are dominated by dispersive plasmons. The observation of selective coupling to even-ordered phonons and stark contrast with the Raman spectra indicate anomalous electron-phonon coupling beyond the Franck-Condon picture. One intriguing possibility is the existence of locally paired quasiparticles in insulating cuprates.
summary: This experimental work uses Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering to probe high-order phonon excitations in the cuprate superconductor La2-xSr_xCuO4. The findings reveal selective coupling to even-ordered phonons, which deviates from simple theoretical expectations. This suggests exotic electronic behavior, potentially involving locally paired quasiparticles, that influences the superconducting state.
main_problem: The study aims to uncover a new regime of electron-phonon coupling in the cuprate superconductor La2-xSr_xCuO4 by analyzing high-order phonon excitations.
main_result: The researchers observed sharp, non-dispersive peaks corresponding to two-phonon and four-phonon excitations, suggesting anomalous electron-phonon coupling beyond the standard Franck-Condon picture.
method: The primary method employed was Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS) at the O K-edge, complemented by comparison with Raman spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The physical system is La2-xSr_xCuO4, a prototypical p-type cuprate superconductor. The analysis focuses on the coupling between charge carriers and lattice vibrations, particularly the in-plane Cu-O bond stretching mode.
key_observables: Phonon excitation energies (e.g., 85 meV, 180 meV, 330 meV), doping dependence of these excitations, and the comparison of RIXS spectra to Raman spectra.
important_parameters: Hole doping concentration (x), which dictates the electronic state, and the energy scale of the phonon modes.
main_assumptions: The anomalous coupling suggests possibilities like the existence of locally paired quasiparticles or bipolarons, moving beyond simple harmonic oscillator models.
figures_summary: Figures show X-ray absorption spectra identifying electronic bands (UHB, ZRS) and RIXS color plots mapping low-energy excitations versus momentum for various dopings, contrasting with Raman spectra.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents RIXS measurements across different doping levels, identifying specific phonon features ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$) and tracking their evolution. It compares these findings to established Raman data to argue for an anomalous coupling mechanism.
why_interesting: The investigation into high-order phonon coupling and its selective nature provides crucial experimental constraints on theoretical models of pairing mechanisms in high-Tc superconductors, which are central to strongly correlated electron physics.
